saw.short: “Scientists reveal the hi” cat becomes the recaption meme of the month
saw.headline: “Scientists reveal the hi” is the *recaption meme* of the month
saw.what: It started with a May 2025 BBC thumbnail asking “What makes ginger cats ginger?”. A “hi” edit appeared in May, and this month recaption edits are spreading on Instagram and TikTok. An inverted “bye” edit posted on 12 Oct got 35,000+ likes in three days.
saw.why: A swap-the-caption template anyone can join. Brands can play with it using their own product in place of the cat.

saw.short: Welsh singer Jamie Miller's “Babydoll” takes over TikTok dance feeds
saw.headline: Jamie Miller's “Babydoll” takes over *TikTok dance feeds*
saw.what: The Welsh singer released Babydoll on 7 Aug. A dance video by @shelbanddyl, posted on 28 Sept, has 7.6M+ views and 671,500 likes in about three weeks. Jennifer Love Hewitt has posted a piano cover.
saw.why: A UK artist's song is driving a global dance trend. The easy routine makes it simple to copy.

saw.short: An artist sketches friends in a Belfast pub, and their reaction goes viral
saw.headline: A sketch of friends in a *Belfast pub* goes viral
saw.what: Live illustrator Geraldine Sawyer (@gertiesoybean) drew a group of friends at the Sunflower Public House in Belfast. The video of their reaction got hundreds of thousands of views in a few days. The friends hung the portrait at Bodega Bagels, where they work.
saw.why: Wholesome, real-life surprise moments still travel. The reaction is the content.

saw.short: A real Paris metro video gets accused of being AI
saw.headline: A real Paris metro video gets *accused of being AI*
saw.what: Océane, 20, taped her iPhone to the outside of a packed train at a Paris metro station and posted the clip on Thursday. Many commenters said it was AI. Her reply: “It's so well done that you think it's AI?”
saw.why: “Is it AI?” is now the first reaction to anything surprising. Real footage needs proof it's real.

platform.short: YouTube tests new bonuses for Shorts creators, including in the UK
platform.headline: YouTube tests *Shorts bonuses*, including in the UK
platform.what: YouTube is testing bonuses for invited Shorts creators in the US, UK, Germany, Brazil, Japan and South Korea. It hasn't published the requirements. Shopping affiliates can also earn bonus commission on videos kept public for 30+ days.
platform.why: More reasons for creators to post Shorts, and to keep shoppable videos up longer.

platform.short: Instagram's chief says more AI labels are coming
platform.headline: Instagram's chief says *more AI labels* are coming
platform.what: Adam Mosseri says Instagram will add more AI labels and is working to stop AI copying creators' work. He also said: “We do not throttle the reach of AI content just for being AI content.”
platform.why: Labels are spreading, but AI posts aren't being held back. Being clearly real is becoming a selling point.

platform.short: Pinterest adds a Barbie DreamHouse style to Restyle
platform.headline: Pinterest adds *Barbie DreamHouse* to Restyle
platform.what: Restyle now has a Barbie DreamHouse option, one of five styles. Pinterest says searches for “Barbie DreamHouse aesthetic” are up 72%. It's a beta for English-language Pinners in the US and Canada.
platform.why: Pinterest is turning aesthetic trends into tools. Not in the UK yet.
